purpose: Deep Christianity research layer: primary biblical source material, canon history, core Christian ideas, historical development, churches and denominations, doctrinal differences, worship and practice, demographics, geography, institutions, and relationships to the wider World and Potatoverse. This layer expands the existing religion work without changing the canonical tree order.
epistemic_rule: Keep biblical text, historical claims, denominational self-description, scholarly reconstruction, demographic measurement, comparative interpretation, and Potatoverse symbolism distinct.

primary_source_plan.license_status: Public domain according to the translation's official site
primary_source_plan.reason: Allows the repository to preserve a complete modern-English biblical text without relying on a copyrighted modern translation.
primary_source_plan.repository_strategy: Treat the Bible as source material, not as a single undifferentiated doctrine database. Preserve book, chapter, verse, canon, translation, and textual-context metadata so later analysis can point back to exact passages.
primary_source_plan.copyright_rule: Do not mix copyrighted translations into the vendored public-domain text. Store copyrighted translations only as bibliographic references or short quotations within applicable limits.

bible_structure.new_testament_core: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, Acts, Romans through Philemon, Hebrews, James, 1-2 Peter, 1-3 John, Jude, Revelation
bible_structure.deuterocanon: Catholic and Orthodox traditions include additional books or passages not contained in the standard Protestant 66-book canon; Orthodox canons differ among traditions.
bible_structure.canon_warning: There is no single Christian Bible table that perfectly represents every church. Canon itself is a historical and denominational relationship to texts.

christian_core.identity: A family of traditions centered on Jesus Christ and the claim that God acts decisively through his life, death and resurrection.
shared_center: hope of resurrection and final renewal
major_theological_questions: What went wrong with humanity and creation?
How are scripture and tradition related?
What happens at death and at the end of history?
christian_core.gospel_summary: In broad Christian usage, the gospel is the good news concerning Jesus Christ: his proclamation of God's kingdom, his death, resurrection and exaltation, and the call to faith, repentance, baptism/discipleship and participation in a renewed people of God. Different traditions explain atonement, justification, sacramental participation and salvation differently.
christian_core.doctrinal_boundary: Shared Christian language does not mean identical theology. Trinity, Christology, salvation, church authority, sacraments, predestination, saints, icons, scripture/tradition and eschatology all contain substantial internal variation.

historical_spine.importance: Christianity emerges from Jewish scripture, worship, messianic expectation and apocalyptic traditions.
Jesus' ministry, crucifixion and resurrection proclamation form the movement's center.
Communities, letters, gospels, worship patterns, leadership structures and debates develop across the Mediterranean and Near East.
Christianity becomes legally favored in the Roman Empire; councils articulate Trinitarian and Christological formulas amid major disputes.
Distinct Latin, Greek, Syriac, Coptic, Armenian, Ethiopian and other traditions develop; communion boundaries harden.
Communion between the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox worlds breaks down, with long prior political and theological development.
Western Christianity fragments further around scripture, justification, sacraments, church authority and reform of ecclesial institutions.
Catholic reform and Protestant confessionalization produce durable institutional and doctrinal traditions.
Christianity expands through missions, migration, colonialism, local agency and new indigenous churches.
Pentecostal and charismatic forms become a major global force, especially in Africa, Latin America and parts of Asia.
Christianity is increasingly global, institutionally diverse and geographically concentrated outside historic European centers.

denomination_map.rule: Use 'family/tradition' for broad historical bodies and 'denomination/church' for specific organized communities. Do not force every Christian group into Protestant/Catholic/Orthodox boxes.

families.name: Roman Catholic Church
families.authority_pattern: scripture + sacred tradition + episcopal teaching office; pope and bishops

families.name: Eastern Orthodox churches
families.authority_pattern: scripture within Holy Tradition; bishops in conciliar communion; no universal pope

families.name: Oriental Orthodox churches
families.authority_pattern: ancient apostolic episcopal traditions and scripture within received tradition

families.name: Anglican Communion and Anglican traditions
families.authority_pattern: scripture, tradition and reason interpreted through national churches and bishops

families.name: Lutheran traditions
families.authority_pattern: scripture as primary doctrinal norm within confessional tradition

families.name: Reformed/Presbyterian traditions
families.authority_pattern: scripture as supreme norm; confessional and synodical traditions vary

families.name: Methodist/Wesleyan traditions
families.authority_pattern: scripture interpreted through tradition, reason and experience in varying formulations

families.name: Anabaptist/Mennonite traditions
families.authority_pattern: scripture read through discipleship and community

families.name: Pentecostal and charismatic traditions
families.authority_pattern: scripture with strong emphasis on present work of the Holy Spirit

families.name: Restorationist traditions
families.authority_pattern: attempts to restore early-church patterns from scripture

families.name: Independent and indigenous African, Asian and Latin American churches

boundary_movements.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
boundary_movements.classification: Christian-origin movement with distinct additional scriptures and theology; classification as Christian is accepted by adherents but disputed by some other Christian traditions
distinctives: Book of Mormon and additional scripture

boundary_movements.name: Jehovah's Witnesses
boundary_movements.classification: Christian-origin movement with non-Trinitarian theology; self-identifies as Christian while many churches classify it outside Nicene Christianity

boundary_movements.name: Unitarian and liberal Christian traditions
boundary_movements.classification: Christian traditions that reject or reinterpret classical Trinitarian formulations
distinctives: ethical and social emphasis in some communities

axes.question: How are Jesus' divinity and humanity related?
What texts are canonical and how are they interpreted?
What authority does received tradition have?
Who has authority to teach and govern?
Which rites are sacraments/ordinances and what do they accomplish?
Infant or believer baptism? What does baptism signify/do?
Symbolic, spiritual, sacramental, or real-presence account?
How are grace, faith, works, justification, sanctification and perseverance related?
How are divine sovereignty and human freedom related?
What role do saints, Mary and intercession have?
What role do icons, statues and religious images have?
How are bishops, priests/pastors, elders and laypeople organized?
How central are liturgy, preaching, sacraments, spontaneous prayer and music?
What is taught about resurrection, judgment, millennium and final renewal?

practice_map: confession/penance in traditions that practice it

demography.latest_comprehensive_global_estimate: 2.3 billion Christians in 2020, 28.8% of world population, according to Pew Research Center's 2025 global religious landscape analysis.
demography.growth_2010_2020: Christian population increased by about 122 million / 6%, but the Christian share of the global population fell because non-Christians grew faster.
demography.important_shift: Sub-Saharan Africa surpassed Europe as the region containing the largest number of Christians.
demography.measurement_warning: Religious identity is not identical to belief, practice, church attendance or doctrinal conformity. Demographic datasets generally classify people by self-identification.
demography.source: Pew Research Center, How the Global Religious Landscape Changed From 2010 to 2020, published 2025

ecumenism.world_council_of_churches: The World Council of Churches describes itself as a fellowship of 356 churches in more than 120 countries representing over 580 million Christians; this is a participating-church measure, not a count of all Christians worldwide.
ecumenism.goal: visible Christian unity, common witness, dialogue and service
ecumenism.scope_warning: The WCC does not include the Roman Catholic Church as a member, although the Catholic Church participates in ecumenical structures and cooperation. Therefore WCC membership must not be treated as the global Christian total.

christianity_to_canonical_tree.separation: creation/fall, heaven-earth, spirit-matter, life-death, identity and covenant distinctions
christianity_to_canonical_tree.ladder: biblical ascent/descent, temple, mountain, covenant history, discipleship and transformation
christianity_to_canonical_tree.door: Christ as threshold/interface is a project interpretation grounded in Christian threshold imagery; it is not a claim that Christianity literally teaches the project's Door ontology
christianity_to_canonical_tree.son: Jesus Christ, Son of Man, Son of God, Messiah/Christ, crucifixion, resurrection
christianity_to_canonical_tree.tree-of-life: Genesis and Revelation provide major biblical Tree of Life anchors; later Christian theology develops resurrection, new creation and participation imagery
christianity_to_canonical_tree.tree-of-strife: sin, death, exile, violence, false worship, judgment and broken communion can be mapped comparatively, but the Tree of Strife remains project mythology rather than a Christian canonical doctrine
christianity_to_canonical_tree.potato: material embodiment, bread/food/agriculture and ordinary creation can be used for Potatoverse analogies, but Potatoism is not Christian doctrine
christianity_to_canonical_tree.world: Christianity becomes a historical civilization-scale network of people, institutions, art, law, education, charity, states, economics, migration and conflict
christianity_to_canonical_tree.north-programme: Christian populations, churches, schools, charities, heritage, political movements and demographic change can be mapped country by country without assuming Christian institutions speak with one political voice

safety_and_integrity: Do not infer a person's beliefs, guilt, extremism, political position or moral character merely from Christian affiliation, denomination, attendance or association. Treat historical controversies as case graphs with claims, evidence, findings and unresolved questions separated.
